title: Alvar Aalto's birth chart
metaDescription: Alvar Aalto's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.7° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 7.1° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 14.7° into Aquarius — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 20.1° Capricorn, Venus was at 11.6° Aquarius, Mars was at 24.5° Capricorn. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that begins as conversation; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Saturn — a sextile holding at 0.4°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Venus sextile Saturn at 1.1°, and Venus trine Pluto at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: the Sun, Jupiter, Pluto close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. The Sun in Aquarius at 14.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Cancer at 7.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Capricorn at 24.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 5 air, 2 earth, 2 fire, 1 water by element and 4 cardinal, 4 mutable, 2 fixed by mode. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 7.1°.
